The method solves for the intersection parameter $t$ of a ray with direction $v$ passing through the origin, intersecting the boundary of a Gaussian defined by mean $\mu$ and covariance $\Sigma$ [S1].

The claim states that the method solves for the intersection parameter $t$ of a ray with direction $v$ passing through the origin, intersecting the boundary of a Gaussian defined by mean $μ$ and covariance $Σ$. The evidence explicitly provides the quadratic equation $at^2 + bt + c = 0$ for finding $t$, where the coefficients $a, b, c$ are defined using $v, μ, Σ$. The equation $v^T Σ^{-1} v t^2 - 2 v^T Σ^{-1} μ t + μ^T Σ^{-1} μ - 1 = 0$ corresponds to the boundary of the ellipsoid defined by one standard deviation of the Gaussian (i.e., $(x-μ)^T Σ^{-1} (x-μ) = 1$). Since the ray passes through the origin, $x = tv$, leading to the derived quadratic. The evidence confirms all components of the claim: the ray definition (origin, direction $v$), the Gaussian parameters ($μ, Σ$), and the solution for $t$ via the specified quadratic form.
